marks.gloss_en: one who roofed over an alleyway that has a side-post -- it is valid
one who roofed over the boards around wells -- it is valid
had he taught us the alleyway, [I would say it is valid] because there are two proper walls; but the boards around wells, where there are not two proper walls -- say no
and had he taught us the boards around wells, [I would say] because there is the name of four walls; but roofing over an alleyway, where there is not the name of four walls -- say no
and had he taught us these two, [they go] from strict to lenient; but from lenient to strict -- say no; [so all three are] needed
רבי -- דתניא: כל סוכה שאין בה ארבע אמות על ארבע אמות פסולה
Rabbi: any sukkah without four amot by four amot is invalid (cited again at 7b.20)
רבי יאשיה -- הא דאמרן: the 7b.7 baraita (kind svara: no kind names a back-reference)
רבי יהודה -- דתנן: סוכה שהיא גבוהה למעלה מעשרים אמה פסולה, רבי יהודה מכשיר (kind tanya_kevatei stands in for a bare דתנן)
the mishnah: a sukkah higher than twenty amot is invalid (same content as sukkah_2a_gubhah_sukkah's p_mishnah_psul)
ורבי שמעון -- דתניא: שתים כהלכתן ושלישית אפילו טפח; רבי שמעון אומר: שלש כהלכתן ורביעית אפילו טפח
the baraita's first view: two walls in the standard sense and a third even of a tefach
רבן גמליאל -- דתניא: העושה סוכתו בראש העגלה או בראש הספינה, רבן גמליאל פוסל ורבי עקיבא מכשיר
one who makes his sukkah atop a wagon or atop a ship: Rabban Gamliel invalidates
בית שמאי -- דתנן: מי שהיה ראשו ורובו בסוכה ושולחנו בתוך הבית, בית שמאי פוסלין ובית הלל מכשירין
one whose head and most of his body were in the sukkah and his table inside the house: Beit Shammai invalidate
רבי אליעזר -- דתנן: העושה סוכתו כמין צריף או שסמכה לכותל, רבי אליעזר פוסל לפי שאין לה גג, וחכמים מכשירין
one who makes his sukkah like a tzrif (a sloping hut), or leans it against a wall: R' Eliezer invalidates
אחרים -- דתניא: סוכה העשויה כשובך פסולה, לפי שאין לה זויות
Acherim: a sukkah made like a dovecote is invalid
מכדי גברא באמתא יתיב, כל שיש בהקיפו שלשה טפחים יש בו רוחב טפח -- בתריסר סגי? a man sits in an amah and circumference is three times width: twelve should suffice for four amot across
the reckoning's premise: a man sits in an amah (reasserted by Rav Asi at 8a.8: לעולם גברא באמתא יתיב)
the mishnah: a sukkah whose sunlight exceeds its shade is invalid
the baraita's first view: 'its sunlight' means sunlight through the sekhakh, not through the walls
Abaye: R' Yoshiya's reason is the verse 'and you shall screen (vesakota) the ark with the curtain' -- the curtain is a partition, and the Torah calls it sekhakh
and the Rabbis? that verse [teaches] that one bends [the curtain] a little, so that it looks like sekhakh
Abaye: Rabbi holds a sukkah must be a fixed dwelling
R' Yochanan: a furnace-shaped (round) sukkah is valid if its circumference has room for twenty-four people to sit, otherwise invalid
like whom? like Rabbi, who requires four amot by four
